# `start_batch_stack`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Start the batch stacking worker over the configured input list.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xda960, StartBatchStack @0x3a6190, parseBatchStartType @0xda680 (64-bit build); firmware 9.75 comet limit and preflight from resolver report E (StartBatchStack @0x3eba10, BatchStackFunc @0x3f3840, FindFirstBatchCometFrame @0x3e8990) |

Stops the AVI reader, resets the global batch status and progress, stores the selected task and frame type, installs the progress formatter and starts the BatchStack worker thread asynchronously. The input list is configured separately (see get_batch_stack_setting) and no hardware-open check is made here; the worker can fail later, for example on an empty list, since there is no immediate empty-list check. A success reply means the worker was started. In the 32-bit build only an optional object with frame_type is read (omitted or {} defaults to light; null, array or scalar gives 107; a non-string frame_type gives 105), task_type is ignored and the deepsky task is always started; its deeper error codes are unresolved. Firmware 9.75, app 3.4.0 (64-bit build) limits the comet task to 200 input frames, checked at start (204) and again in the worker on the input list and on the expanded list (err_code 204; how worker failures reach the BatchStack event is unresolved). A new comet preflight finds the first frame with a comet and fails with 9005 if none, 9002 if its detector cannot start; too few candidates give 9004. The comet list is separate from the deepsky list, and its key_frame is the reference frame. The star-trail task honours the list's batch_startrails_mode (0 maximum video, 1 decay video, 2 both). While running, the worker reports function-state events whose payload adds percent (number), frame_type and task_type (strings), stacked_img and total_img (integers), remaining_sec (integer, only when non-negative; INFERRED seconds), input_thn (string, when non-empty) and output_file (an object, when available); the producer of output_file members and the exact Event name are unresolved.

Side effects: Stops the AVI reader, resets batch status and progress, and starts the BatchStack worker thread, which reads the input list and writes result files.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"start_batch_stack"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | no | - | Parameters of start_batch_stack as parsed by the 64-bit build. Omitted params default to task deepsky with frame type light. A supplied non-object (null, array, scalar) is rejected with 107. A supplied object must contain at least one of task_type and frame_type ({} is rejected with 105); each supplied key must be a string; a missing counterpart defaults to 0 (deepsky, light). Unknown keys are ignored. No numeric exposure or file-list keys exist. The 32-bit build differs: see the method description. [READ] |
| `params.task_type` | string | no | deepsky | Batch task: deepsky, startrail_image, startrail_video or comet (case-sensitive, exact). An unknown string is rejected with 102. [READ] |
| `params.frame_type` | string | no | light | Frame type: light, dark, bias or flat (case-insensitive, exact). An unrecognised value maps to an invalid type and is then rejected with 207 for deepsky. The startrail tasks override any supplied value to light; comet requires light (207 otherwise). [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | (success) The request method, echoed. [READ] |
| `result` | integer | yes | - | (success) For these methods the result is the integer 0. Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (success) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (success) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 204 | Firmware 9.75, app 3.4.0, comet task only; the comet input list holds more than 200 frames (the comet_max_frame_num constant). The err_code is stored under the batch lock and the start fails; that this code is the reply is INFERRED from the stored err_code | `out of limit` |
| 107 | params supplied but not an object | `expected object param` |
| 105 | Object has neither selector, or a supplied selector is not a string | `expected string param` |
| 102 | task_type is an unknown string | `invalid params` |
| 207 | Invalid task and frame combination (for example comet with a non-light frame, or an unrecognised frame_type for deepsky) | `fail to operate` |
| 524 | A stack status is active or a dark-frame creation function is running | `function conflict` |
| 536 | A ViewPlan worker is running | `view plan is already running` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Errors from starting the named worker are forwarded with their own codes and are not enumerated.

## Example

Request, omitted:

```json
{"id":131,"method":"start_batch_stack"}
```

Request, comet:

```json
{"id":132,"method":"start_batch_stack","params":{"task_type":"comet","frame_type":"light"}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"start_batch_stack","result":0,"code":0,"id":131}
```

Reply, plan-running:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"start_batch_stack","error":"view plan is already running","code":536,"id":133}
```
